Golden fixtures for `swiftshot verify`, shared by the Swift and the JVM implementation. Each case
directory holds the inputs (`baseline/` with `baseline.json`, `output/` with
`swiftshot-report.json`, `config.json` with the comparison settings) and the expected report files
(`expected/result.json`, `expected/junit.xml`, `expected/manifest.json`, `expected/summary.md`, `expected/index.html`, and `expected/images/`,
generated by the engine). Run verify with `SWIFTSHOT_COMMIT=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567`,
`SWIFTSHOT_BRANCH=feature/x`, `SWIFTSHOT_VERSION_OVERRIDE=1.0.0-test` and `SWIFTSHOT_CI=false`; every output must match
byte for byte, and the exit code must follow `status` (passed 0, failed 1, error 2). The format is
[docs/wiki/Baseline-format.md](../../../docs/wiki/Baseline-format.md); `python3 -I make.py`
regenerates everything except `expected/images/`, which the JVM engine writes
(`SWIFTSHOT_WRITE_FIXTURE_IMAGES=1` on `CompareTest`) and `make.py` checks pixel and byte for byte.
The case `empty-run` (a report with no screenshots and no errors) expects `status: "error"` with the
unattributed error `The run rendered no screenshots` and no removals; both implementations count 28 cases.
A case may have `env.json`, merged over the standard environment above (an object of strings; `null`
removes a variable), and files it refers to. A path in `env.json` is relative to the case directory.
The case `ci-github` removes `SWIFTSHOT_COMMIT`, `SWIFTSHOT_BRANCH` and `SWIFTSHOT_CI` and sets a GitHub
pull request run with `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH=event.json`: its report records the pull request's head commit
from `event.json` and `"ci": {"buildUrl", "provider": "github", "pullRequest": "7"}`. The detection
cases are in [../ci](../ci).
The cases `hostile-ids` and `hostile-run-error` put markup, quotes, URL and shell metacharacters, non-ASCII and an id with a comma into every field `index.html` shows.
`index.html` is `Shared/report.html` with `result.json` in it; `make.py` refreshes that template's Content-Security-Policy hashes, so run it after editing the template.
The case `summary-truncation` has 300 added 1x1 images with ~300-byte ids (`en-US/<D*100>-<P*100>/<Q*100><index>`: a path part stays under the file systems' 255 bytes), so the 200-row cap and the 60,000-byte cap both apply.
